title: Decorators
summary: Wrap functions to add behaviour without touching them.

steps.title: Functions that take functions
body: A **decorator** is a function that takes a function and returns a new one that wraps it:
`*args, **kwargs` let the wrapper accept and forward any arguments at all.

steps.explain: `twice` returns a new function; `add3` itself is unchanged.

steps.title: The @ syntax
body: `@decorator` above a `def` is shorthand for `name = decorator(name)`:
It plays the role of an ASP.NET filter or attribute that runs code around an action, but it is ordinary code you can read. Common uses: logging, timing, caching, retries, access checks.

steps.prompt: Arrange the lines into a decorator that prints `calling NAME` before each call.

steps.explain: Stacked decorators apply bottom-up: `word = bracket(stars(word))`. So stars wraps first, then brackets go around that.

options: So the decorated function keeps its `__name__` and docstring
It is required or the decorator will not run
steps.explain: Without it, every decorated function reports its name as `wrapper`, which confuses debugging, logging and test tools.

steps.title: Decorators with arguments
body: To write `@repeat(3)`, add one more layer: a function that takes the arguments and **returns a decorator**.

steps.title: Count the calls
prompt: Write a decorator `counted` that counts how many times the decorated function is called. Store the count on the wrapper as an attribute `calls` (functions are objects, so `wrapper.calls = 0` works). Keep the original name with `functools.wraps`.
template: Dojo.eq("each function has its own count", 1, add.calls)
hints: Set `wrapper.calls = 0` after defining `wrapper`, before returning it.

steps.title: Validate arguments
prompt: Write a decorator factory `positive(*names)` so that `@positive("qty", "price")` raises `ValueError` if any of those **keyword** arguments is passed as a number `<= 0`. Otherwise it calls the function normally.
solution: if n in kwargs and kwargs[n] <= 0:
template: Dojo.eq("valid call works", "2 x tea @ 1.5", order("tea", qty=2, price=1.5))
Dojo.eq("defaults still work", "1 x jam @ 1.0", order("jam"))
Dojo.throws("qty=0 raises ValueError", ValueError, lambda: order("tea", qty=0))
Dojo.throws("price=-1 raises ValueError", ValueError, lambda: order("tea", price=-1))
hints: Check `if n in kwargs and kwargs[n] <= 0: raise ValueError(...)`.
